findings.title: Four interface comments and two test helper remarks disagree with the source, and none of them changes who can move funds
findings.difference: None. These are differences between the source text and the repository's own comments, tests and test doubles. They are the same on every network.
findings.mechanism: This unit compared every NatSpec sentence in src/interfaces with the function it describes and read every helper in src/test and test/utils. Six statements do not match the source, in addition to the four recorded in F-006. First, src/interfaces/IHooks.sol:102 says the fee returned by beforeSwap is used only if it is at most 1,000,000. The source reverts with LPFeeTooLarge when the override flag is set and the fee is above the maximum (src/libraries/Pool.sol:303-305, src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:75-78). The test agrees with the source and expects the revert (test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol:151-162), although its own comment says the large fee is not used. Second, IHooks.sol:50 and IHooks.sol:81 describe the delta handed to afterAddLiquidity and afterRemoveLiquidity as the sum of principal, fees and hook delta. The source passes principal plus fees, and subtracts the hook delta only after the hook returns (src/PoolManager.sol:171-178, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:219-243). The test doubles rely on the source behaviour (src/test/FeeTakingHook.sol:54-91, test/CustomAccounting.t.sol:270-322). Third, src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:85-86 calls the Swap event amounts the deltas of the pool's balances. The emitted values are the swapper's deltas, negative for the amount paid in (src/PoolManager.sol:241-250), and the tests expect -100 and 98 for an exact input of 100 (test/PoolManager.t.sol:500-503). Fourth, IPoolManager.sol:174 says take reverts if the requested amount is not available. That holds for native currency and for tokens with code, and test/PoolManager.t.sol:917-922 states it for an empty manager. For a currency address without code the transfer call succeeds with empty return data and nothing moves (src/types/Currency.sol:60-74), which earlier cycles recorded under assumption A4. Fifth, test/utils/CurrencySettler.sol:20-25 settles native currency without a prior sync and says a sync is not required, while the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 tells integrators to call sync before a native settle. A native settle that follows a token sync by other code in the same transaction reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:353-356, test/PoolManager.t.sol:976-989). Sixth, src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol:27-33 offers setIsUnlocked and an _isUnlocked override, no test calls setIsUnlocked, and collectProtocolFees never reads the lock (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). This is the test double side of the first item of F-006. I traced each item for a fund effect. A hook that returns an oversized fee can only stop swaps in its own pool. The delta seen by a liquidity hook is the amount the hook can charge against, and the caller delta plus the hook delta still equals the pool delta in every replayed case. The event wording affects readers of logs only. The native settle revert needs code that runs earlier in the same transaction, and it returns the caller's value with the revert.
findings.impact: No loss or freeze found. A hook author who trusts IHooks.sol:102 may ship a hook that makes swaps in its own pool revert when it computes a fee above 100 percent. An integrator that copies the native branch of the test helper without sync(address(0)) can have a native settle reverted by a token sync left earlier in the same transaction.
findings.preconditions: None for the comments. The native settle revert needs a call to sync with a token address earlier in the same transaction, for example from a hook of a pool the caller used or from a contract that bundles several actions.
findings.mitigations: Correct the six texts. Hook authors should cap the fee before setting the override flag. Integrators should call sync(address(0)) before every native settle, as the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 says.

sources.supports: Comment says an override fee above the maximum is not used.
The source validates the override fee and reverts with LPFeeTooLarge when it is above 1,000,000.
The test expects LPFeeTooLarge for an override fee of 1,000,001.
Comment says the delta passed to afterAddLiquidity includes the hook delta. Line 81 says the same for removal.
The hook receives the delta before the hook delta is subtracted.
Comment describes the Swap event amounts as pool balance deltas.
The test expects amount0 -100 and amount1 98 for an exact input of 100 of currency0.
The helper settles native currency without calling sync first.
Comment says integrators should call sync before a native settle.
The test double has a lock toggle that no test uses.

cleared.check: test/PoolManager.t.sol, every asserted number. Replayed on a Python transcription of Pool, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickMath, TickBitmap, Position, Hooks and PoolManager, with the TickMath constants parsed from the source file, and with the test routers of src/test transcribed including their require statements.
cleared.result: All hold. The Swap events at lines 500-503 and 517-527 come out as (-100, 98, 79228162514264329749955861424, 1e18, -1, 3000) for the token pool and the native pool. The event at line 608 comes out as (-10, 8, 79228162514264336880490487708, 1e18, -1, 100). The ERC-6909 amounts are 98 minted, 27 burned for an exact output of 25, and 71 left, for the token and the native case (lines 659-751). Donating 100 and 200 to liquidity of 1e18 gives fee growth 34028236692093846346337 and 68056473384187692692674 (lines 841-864). With the protocol fee at 1000 pips in both directions, a swap of 10000 accrues 10 for exact input, exact output, the opposite direction and the native pool (lines 1041-1171). The fuzz test at lines 779-819 held in 4,000 random runs over protocol fees from 0 to 1000 and amounts from 1 wei to the int256 limits: the accrued fee equals the input times the fee divided by 1e6, rounded down, and nothing accrues in the other currency or on liquidity changes. The router assertions on delta signs and on equality of the returned delta with the transient delta never failed.

cleared.check: test/PoolManager.t.sol, all 27 expectRevert cases and the hook call assertions, read against the order of checks in the source.
cleared.result: All name the error the source raises first. A call outside an unlock fails with ManagerLocked before any pool check (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99, 147, 189, 258, 291, 300, 322, 332). Inside an unlock an uninitialized pool fails with PoolNotInitialized before any hook runs (154, 196, 264). A hook that returns a wrong selector gives InvalidHookResponse at the before hook and, once that is fixed, at the after hook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154). donate on a pool without liquidity gives NoLiquidityToReceiveFees (src/libraries/Pool.sol:468). A token that returns false makes take revert with WrappedError(token, transfer selector, 32 zero bytes, ERC20TransferFailed), and I checked the byte layout written by bubbleUpAndRevertWith against the ABI encoding the test builds (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:83-119, src/types/Currency.sol:64-86). The recorded hook arguments match what Hooks.sol encodes: msg.sender first, then the PoolKey, the parameters, the delta before any hook delta, a zero fee delta and the hook data (Hooks.sol:178-245, 256, 300). A second unlock from the callback or from another contract reverts with AlreadyUnlocked (PoolManager.sol:105).

cleared.check: test/PoolManager.swap.t.sol. The two fuzz tests require a v4 swap to give the same amounts as a Uniswap v3 pool created from the bytecode fixture test/bin/v3Factory.bytecode. I wrote a small EVM interpreter in Python, deployed the fixture in it, created pools through the factory, and compared v3 mint and swap results with the transcription of src for random fees, tick spacings, prices, positions and amounts drawn as the test helpers in src/test/Fuzzers.sol draw them.
cleared.result: All hold. In 8,920 cases the transcription of src and the v3 pool agreed: 8,639 cases gave equal swap amounts in both currencies and the same price, tick and in range liquidity afterwards, 235 cases had a v3 amount outside int128 and the v4 side reverted with SafeCastOverflow, which is the outcome the test accepts, and 46 cases were skipped by the helper's assume on a zero liquidity bound. 6,320 of the cases used one position and compared the mint amounts as well, and 2,600 used zero to six positions with the tight liquidity bound of the second test. Fees ran from 0 to 999,999, tick spacings from 1 to 16,383, amounts from 1 to 2^127 - 1 in both directions and both swap types, with the price limit one unit inside the price range. No case diverged and no v3 call reverted. The transcription uses the test router's require statements, so the delta signs and the equality of the returned delta with the transient delta were checked in every case. The interpreter has no gas accounting, which does not affect amounts. This is a replay on a transcription and does not test the compiled contract.

All hold. The fuzz test expects the reverts in the order tick spacing too large, tick spacing too small, currencies out of order or equal, hook address not valid, fee too large, which is the order of src/PoolManager.sol:119-128. The zero hook address with the dynamic fee flag is rejected as HookAddressNotValid before the fee is looked at (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:124-126). The Initialize event carries the tick from getTickAtSqrtPrice and is emitted before afterInitialize (PoolManager.sol:134-141). A second initialize reverts with PoolAlreadyInitialized (src/libraries/Pool.sol:101). The hook receives (msg.sender, PoolKey, sqrtPriceX96) and (msg.sender, PoolKey, sqrtPriceX96, tick). Spacing 32767 is accepted, 32768, 0 and -1 are rejected with the value as argument.

cleared.check: test/ModifyLiquidity.t.sol. The ffi tests compare modifyLiquidity amounts with a JavaScript reference. I did not run the bundled script. I rebuilt its formula from test/js-scripts/src (sqrt price from 1.0001^tick in decimal arithmetic, then the rounded up amount formulas) in Python and applied the test's one pip tolerance.
cleared.result: All hold. The fixed case with spacing 32767 gives (-16763964227853053397, -16787892583597717024) from the source formulas and the same from the reference formula. The fixed case with spacing 1 and range 10 to 17 gives (-322770984484567984193, 0) from both. 3,000 random positions drawn as createFuzzyLiquidityParams draws them on the 1:1 pool with spacing 60 were all within one pip. The salt tests follow from the position hash over owner, ticks and salt (src/libraries/Position.sol:48-67): two salts and two routers give four separate positions, and the liquidity read back equals the sum of the deltas for that position only.

cleared.check: test/Sync.t.sol, test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol and the take, settle, mint, burn and fee collection cases of test/PoolManager.t.sol, replayed as action sequences on the transcription with the native ERC-20 face of src/test/NativeERC20.sol modelled as a token whose balance is the native balance.
cleared.result: All 30 replayed sequences behave as the tests state. sync outside an unlock sets the synced currency. The reserves getter returns 0 when no token is synced, also after sync(address(0)), although the stored number stays (src/libraries/TransientStateLibrary.sol:18-21). A settle with no payment applies no delta. A token sent without sync is not credited and a later sync, transfer and settle credits only the later transfer, so the first 10 units stay in the manager (Sync.t.sol:207-253). settleFor credits the named account, for 302 amounts up to 2^127 - 1 and three kinds of taker including the manager itself. A native settle after a token sync reverts with NonzeroNativeValue, and after sync(address(0)) it credits msg.value. A second settle credits nothing. clear reverts with MustClearExactPositiveDelta for a negative delta, for an amount above, below or zero against a positive delta, and for a nonzero amount against a zero delta, and it clears an exact positive delta and lowers the nonzero delta count to 0. collectProtocolFees reverts with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced for the synced token in both lock states, and an amount of 0 collects everything accrued. With the face token I found no order of sync, settle and take in which one payment is credited twice: a credit under the face id needs a rise of the native balance after sync, and a native credit needs msg.value with no token synced (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). An exhaustive search to depth 10 over 23 actions of one account inside an unlock (sync of either id, settle with a value of 0 to 2, take of either id, a transfer in through the face, a forced native send, mint and burn of claims of either id, clear) visited 526,043 distinct states and found no state with zero deltas in which the account held more native currency plus claims than at the start.

cleared.check: test/CustomAccounting.t.sol, all nine tests, with the four hook doubles (FeeTakingHook, LPFeeTakingHook, CustomCurveHook, DeltaReturningHook) transcribed and driven through the transcription of Hooks.sol and PoolManager.sol.
cleared.result: All hold. Exact input of 1000 gives 998 out and the hook takes 12, so the swapper receives 986. Exact output of 1000 costs 1002 plus 12. The custom curve hook turns an exact input and an exact output of 123456 into a 1:1 exchange with a zero amount pool swap. The liquidity fee hook receives 543/10000 of the principal on add and on removal, and swapper loss minus hook gain equals the manager gain. The fee revenue fuzz (3,000 runs each for add and remove, donations up to (2^128 - 1)/2 and (2^128 - 1)/3) gives the hook the donated amount or one unit less and never more. The delta fuzz at lines 160-266 held in 20,000 runs: SwapAmountCannotBeZero for a zero amount, HookDeltaExceedsSwapAmount exactly when the hook delta would flip the sign of the amount, the hook balance changes by its delta, the swapper balance by the returned delta, and the two constants -6018336102428409 and 5981737760509662 are the exact limits of the pool in both directions. In every run the caller delta plus the hook delta equals the pool delta.

All hold on the transcription. The six expected reverts of DynamicFees.t.sol are raised where the tests say: LPFeeTooLarge(1000001) inside afterInitialize and beforeSwap, wrapped with HookCallFailed, UnauthorizedDynamicLPFeeUpdate for a caller that is not the hook and for a static fee pool, and InvalidFeeForExactOut for an exact output at a fee of 1,000,000 and at 999,999 plus a protocol fee of 1000. The Swap events come out as stated: fee 123 gives (-100, 98, 79228162514264329749955861424, -1), fee 1,000,000 gives (-100, 0, the unchanged price, tick -1), fee 500,000 gives (-100, 49, 79228162514264333632135824623) and (-202, 100, 79228162514264329670727698909), and fee 123 with protocol fee 1000 emits 1123. The fuzz test at DynamicFees.t.sol:286-318 held in 6,000 runs, including the rule that the whole fee goes to the protocol, rounded up, when the LP fee is zero. The return fee fuzz held for 5,015 values of the 24 bit fee: an override above 1,000,000 after removal of the flag reverts with that value, and otherwise the output is within one unit of the input less the fee. A returned fee is not stored, and a static fee pool ignores it (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:263).

cleared.check: test/SkipCallsTestHook.t.sol and test/utils/NestedActions.t.sol: a hook that re-enters the manager with the same action must not be called again, and deltas belong to the direct caller.
cleared.result: All eleven counter expectations hold on the transcription with a re-entering hook double: the counter rises by one per outer action for each of the ten hook flags. The hook's own nested action is accounted to the hook address and skips every hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:171-175, 217, 253, 293). The nested removal leaves the hook owing one unit of each currency from rounding, which satisfies the double's assertion. In the nested action test the executor that calls swap carries the delta (-100, 98) and the contract that called unlock carries none (src/PoolManager.sol:226, src/test/PoolNestedActionsTest.sol:119-143).

cleared.check: test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol, all 29 tests including the value assertions, on a transcription of ERC6909.sol and ERC6909Claims.sol.
cleared.result: All hold in 60,000 random rounds. burnFrom and transferFrom lower a finite allowance by the amount, leave an allowance of 2^256 - 1 unchanged, and do not touch the allowance when the caller is the owner or an operator. A transfer to oneself leaves the balance unchanged. Balance underflow, balance overflow at the receiver, mint overflow and a missing approval all revert, because the arithmetic in ERC6909.sol:25-48 and 79-89 is checked. The unchecked block around the mint in src/PoolManager.sol:323-328 does not reach into _mint. The interface id 0x0f632fb3 in supportsInterface equals the XOR of the seven ERC-6909 selectors, which I recomputed.

cleared.check: test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol, and a function by function reading of src/PoolManager.sol against the two other implementations in the repository, src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol and src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol. I compared them by reading. A diff command on the two files was refused by the session's permission layer, so the comparison is by reading only.
cleared.result: The eight tests hold: a delegatecall into modifyLiquidity, swap or donate of the real manager passes the lock check in the proxy's context and then fails with DelegateCallNotAllowed, because the modifier order is onlyWhenUnlocked then noDelegateCall (src/PoolManager.sol:147-148, 189-190, 258-259, src/NoDelegateCall.sol:24-32). The proxy double differs from the production contract in three places. It puts noDelegateCall on its own unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn (ProxyPoolManager.sol:58, 151, 156, 163, 176, 181), while the production functions carry only the lock check (PoolManager.sol:104, 291, 300, 305, 322, 332). It emits Initialize after afterInitialize (ProxyPoolManager.sol:90-94), while production emits before (PoolManager.sol:139-141). Its sync is public. The proxy forwards take, settle, mint, burn and clear by delegatecall and expects them to run, so the double is consistent with production functions that accept delegatecall. I checked whether the missing modifier matters for funds. A delegatecall runs PoolManager code against the storage, transient storage and balance of the calling contract. The lock flag, the deltas, the claims and every transfer then belong to that contract. Nothing held by the PoolManager can be reached this way. The same holds for an account that points an EIP-7702 delegation at the PoolManager, because the delegated code runs in the context of that account. EIP-7702 says that CALL loads the code at the delegated address and executes it in the context of the authority, and EIP-7 says that the call created by DELEGATECALL has the same sender and value as the original call. I fetched both texts in this session. I did not test how the client of each network implements DELEGATECALL and delegation, so for the 20 networks other than Ethereum this rests on the two specifications. ProtocolFeesImplementation mirrors ProtocolFees without change and adds a lock toggle that nothing reads.

cleared.check: test/Extsload.t.sol, test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.t.sol and test/types/Currency.t.sol, read against the source.
cleared.result: All hold. extsload for a list of slots, for a run of consecutive slots with a length from 0 to 1000, and with trailing bytes appended to the calldata returns an ABI array of the stored words and a length that is a multiple of 32 (src/Extsload.sol:10-63). A length of 0 makes the loop read one slot that the returned range does not include. setProtocolFeeController reverts with the string UNAUTHORIZED for a caller that is not the owner (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:19-23). setProtocolFee checks the caller, then the fee, then the pool, and the fee rule equals both 12 bit halves being at most 1000 (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41, src/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:25-32). collectProtocolFees reverts for an amount above the accrued fees because the subtraction is checked, treats 0 as everything, and leaves the balance unchanged when the recipient is the contract itself. _updateProtocolFees wraps, as the fuzz test expects. Currency: a token that reverts without data gives WrappedError(token, transfer selector, empty, ERC20TransferFailed), a native transfer above the balance gives WrappedError(recipient, zero selector, empty, NativeTransferFailed), and a token that reverts with a panic has the panic bytes passed through (src/types/Currency.sol:40-88). fromId truncates to 160 bits and toId widens.

cleared.check: NatSpec in src/interfaces compared sentence by sentence with the implementation: IPoolManager.sol, IProtocolFees.sol, IHooks.sol, IExtsload.sol, IExttload.sol, callback/IUnlockCallback.sol and external/IERC6909Claims.sol.
cleared.result: Apart from the six items in this unit's finding and the two interface items already in F-006, each sentence matches. Checked in particular: the error descriptions at IPoolManager.sol:16-49 against the places that raise them, tick spacing limited to the int16 maximum, sync as the checkpoint for token payments and sync with the native currency as the way to settle native funds after a token sync (165-171, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), clear requiring the exact positive delta (190-194, PoolManager.sol:310-319), the truncation of ids to 160 bits in mint and burn (196-210), feesAccrued returned for information and callerDelta as principal plus fees less the hook delta (128-132), donate going to the positions in range at slot0.tick (149-155), and the hook return types in IHooks.sol, where a hook delta is read only when the matching return delta flag is set (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:159-168, 266, 301).

cleared.check: Do the tests and test doubles refer to anything the source no longer declares. A changed or removed error, function or library member would stop the test suite from compiling.
cleared.result: No. A script collected the 85 distinct selector references of the form Owner.name.selector in test/ and src/test, and each name is declared as an error, function or event in the repository. Every member called on the manager in the tests exists in src/PoolManager.sol, src/ProtocolFees.sol, src/ERC6909.sol, the two state libraries or Owned, and the three names that do not (burnFrom, setPrice, updateProtocolFees) belong to test doubles. The check is textual and does not replace a compiler.

leads.question: Does the compiled PoolManager, driven through the test routers of src/test on a local chain, give the same deltas, events and revert data as the Python transcription on the cases this unit replayed, in particular the 20,000 hook delta runs of test/CustomAccounting.t.sol:160-266 and the 8,920 cases of the differential against test/bin/v3Factory.bytecode?
leads.why: The transcription follows the source text of PoolManager.sol and Hooks.sol. It cannot show a difference introduced by the compiler, by the via_ir optimiser or by the assembly that copies and parses hook return data, and those parts decide which account is debited. Lead L-024 asks the same for the math libraries only. The check needs forge and nothing outside this repository.

leadResults.answer: The part assigned to this unit is answered and found no new departure with a fund effect. Replayed and satisfied by the source text: test/PoolManager.t.sol (all numbers on a transcription, all 27 expectRevert cases and the hook and initialize cases by reading), test/PoolManager.swap.t.sol (differential against the v3 bytecode fixture in a Python EVM interpreter), test/DynamicFees.t.sol, test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol, test/SkipCallsTestHook.t.sol, test/Extsload.t.sol, test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.t.sol and the transfer cases of test/types/Currency.t.sol. Every NatSpec sentence of IPoolManager.sol, IProtocolFees.sol and IHooks.sol was compared with its function, and six more wording differences without fund effect are recorded in this unit's finding. src/PoolManager.sol was read function by function against src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol and src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol: the proxy adds noDelegateCall to unlock, take, settle, settleFor, mint and burn and emits Initialize after afterInitialize, and neither difference gives access to funds held by the PoolManager. Still open under this lead: the library test files it names (TickMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, FullMath, BitMath, UnsafeMath, StateLibrary, Lock and test/Tick.t.sol), which belong to the unit core-code-tests-replay-libraries, and the bytecode size and creation code hash recorded in snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json for test_bytecodeSize and test_initcodeHash, which need a compiler. The libraries unit of this cycle has filed a lead for that check.

The files of this lead that earlier attempts left open and that fall to this unit are now covered, and the source text satisfies all of them: the liquidity section of test/CustomAccounting.t.sol (fee taking hooks on add and remove, 3,000 fuzz runs each for the LP fee hook), the value assertions of test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol (60,000 random rounds on a transcription), test/ModifyLiquidity.t.sol including the JavaScript reference, whose formula I rebuilt in Python instead of running the bundled script, test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol, test/PoolManagerInitialize.t.sol, test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol, test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol and every expectRevert case of test/PoolManager.t.sol. Not covered by this unit: the hook call sequences of test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol and test/libraries/FullMath.t.sol.
